diagrams.title: Getting Booked by Insurance Relocation Companies
diagrams.subtitle: From portal listing to a signed, utility-capped agreement
diagrams.caption: Five practitioner-tested moves for landing displaced families: list in agency portals, confirm by phone, run specialist email blasts, let the agency name the number, and cap utilities before signing.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Figures are attributed practitioner claims. The $8,100 house versus about $15,000 a month in hotel rooms is one family-of-seven case reported by Jesse Vasquez, not a market average.
diagrams.note: Sources include Bailey Kramer (DFn2vbuykUY, J-7ks576i8Q), The Bougie Baldie (PaAH8z8rPe8), Dr Chau Ong (Bbit4NDO_Hc), and Jesse Vasquez (Ncr7TdF1G34, O1Wmu9p-zdc).

stages.label: List on ALE Solutions and THD
stages.detail: Put a realistic number on the ALE Solutions form; the listed price is not the price you charge and gets renegotiated after the match (Bailey Kramer).

stages.label: Confirm every submission by phone
stages.detail: Call within a week, because the form gives no confirmation and can create duplicate entries (The Bougie Baldie).

stages.label: Email specialists on a cadence
stages.detail: Weekly or biweekly blasts with a PS asking specialists to forward and a PPS offering referrals in other cities, so ten contacts become twenty (Bailey Kramer).

stages.label: Let the agency name the number
stages.detail: Ask for the price range per night, never the budget (Dr Chau Ong). Anchor against the hotel bill, such as $8,100 a month versus about $15,000 in two rooms (Jesse Vasquez).

stages.label: Cap utilities before signing
stages.detail: Write electric and water caps into the agreement and notes, such as the guest paying electric above $500; uncapped electric ran about $1,000 a month on the $8,100 house (Jesse Vasquez).

diagrams.title: The Arbitrage Scale Ladder
diagrams.subtitle: Peak portfolios, delegated growth, and per-building density
diagrams.caption: Reported portfolio sizes from two scaled operators, narrowing from Humza Zafar's 450-unit peak to Richie Matthews' average of 6 units per building.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Each stage is a separately reported operator figure, not a single cohort converting through stages. Unit counts are attributed practitioner claims.
diagrams.note: Humza Zafar (1D3J3ID1ZZM) reported the 450 peak and 300 trim; Richie Matthews (VtVf0h80q0w, O4cBKKUBS64) reported 18 to 35 units in 6 months and the $2,000 to $2,500 minimum net per property.

stages.label: Peak portfolio (Humza Zafar)
stages.detail: Economy units died to competition; stacking units in Detroit cost about $100K in cannibalization.

stages.label: Trimmed A-class portfolio
stages.detail: Shifted to A-class because fixed costs are identical across classes; cleared 0% APR cards before they reset.

stages.label: Delegated portfolio (Richie Matthews)
stages.detail: An $80-a-month Hospitable plus dynamic pricing stack and 900 VA protocols after delegating operations.

stages.label: Pre-delegation portfolio
stages.conversion: Baseline before the March 2021 system build

stages.label: Average units per building
stages.detail: Any property not netting at least $2,000 to $2,500 per month gets dropped or renegotiated.

diagrams.title: ALE Pays Only the Increase
diagrams.subtitle: Rent and meal reimbursement after the normal-cost baseline
diagrams.caption: Two payer-side examples: rent rising from $1,500 to $2,000 pays $500, and a $200 weekly food spend against a $150 baseline pays $50.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The rent and meal segments are separate examples from different speakers and use different periods; the meal figures are weekly. Overstating the normal-expense baseline shortchanges the recovery (Bill Coffman).
diagrams.note: Rent example from United Policyholders (bPQqrGrXfiI); meal example from Kela Trishaan (awTD63In04A); coverage principle from Insurance Savvy (Xnrpk3PKFg4).

diagrams.title: Insurance Housing Against Long-Term and Short-Term Rent
diagrams.subtitle: Metro Atlanta case studies and a Smyrna Coverage D budget
diagrams.caption: Reported monthly figures for the same markets across long-term, short-term, and insurance midterm models, plus a worked Coverage D budget.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Typical values are the figures the speakers stated, not computed midpoints. The Smyrna budget strips roughly 10% land value from a $480K purchase using a cost segregation study.
diagrams.note: Ruben Kanya's Atlanta 4-bedroom figures via Rich Somers (g075AOuQIwk) and Smyrna math via Landlord Diaries - The Monthly Rentals Podcast (vbHlGVZKjvg); Anya Sher's 3/2 via Real Estate Pros Show (-OpbvAckfkQ).

diagrams.title: Landlord Pitch Gates for Rental Arbitrage
diagrams.subtitle: Framing, rent cap, landlord fears, and proving unit one
diagrams.caption: Four gates distilled from operators who pitched hundreds of landlords, including Aurelio Licata's 500+ pitches that produced 50+ properties.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The $2,000 rent against $3,000 charged is Sean Rakidzich's baseline spread rule; Linda Kim's $4,000 ask against a $3,700 need is a single walk-away example.
diagrams.note: Drawn from Aurelio Licata (Q3hSpjquUTE), Rafa Loza (894g1JF-IuM), Sean Rakidzich (lGwvDjwR4uU), Linda Kim (5vV0oy-jJ7g), Jorge Contreras (_M0OdXelhoU), and LoCasa (OSi_ARPIpaM).

nodes.question: Did the pitch open as a corporate housing company with the filter question about short-term furnished leases?
nodes.fail_action: Reframe; never lead with Airbnb, and ask whether the landlord allows leases for short-term furnished housing.

nodes.question: Is the rent low enough to charge roughly double, such as $3,000 against $2,000 rent?
nodes.fail_action: Walk away, as Linda Kim did from a $4,000 ask against a $3,700 need.

nodes.question: Are on-time rent and property condition answered with autopay two days early and written damage responsibility?
nodes.fail_action: Show the autopay confirmation itself instead of arguing the point.

nodes.question: Is unit one profitable before adding unit two?
nodes.pass_next: Sign a two-to-three-year lease under an LLC and bind your own liability and loss-of-income coverage.
nodes.fail_action: Fix unit one first; adding more units does not solve the problem.

diagrams.title: Lease Exit Map for the Leaseholder
diagrams.subtitle: Who sets the exit price when a lease ends early
diagrams.caption: The leaseholder sits between the landlord's buyout terms, legal advice on the duty to re-rent, a replacement-tenant offer, and statutory exits such as SCRA.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Termination fees of 1 to 3 months rent and a buyout around two months rent are typical figures cited by the speakers; Florida caps liquidated damages at two months under Statutes 83.595.
diagrams.note: Drawn from DoorLoop (DMY8aqSWFmQ), Tenant Law Group, PC (mXtFESh8Jwc), 60SecondLaw (X_XeyY10oQE), Adulting Shouldn't Suck (07RfH5S46pg), and Better Call Kal (2ZipHRbP_7U).

center.focus: No move-out and no rent stoppage until a termination agreement states the amount, move-out date, and that no further rent is owed.

spokes.kpi: Buyout around two months rent; fees typically 1 to 3 months
Direction on the state duty to re-rent, often free
Proposed alongside an early-termination penalty offer
Lease ends 30 days after the next rent date; no fees

diagrams.title: Insuring the Rental Operation
diagrams.subtitle: From the conversion call to scheduled portfolio coverage
diagrams.caption: Four steps that move a property off a homeowner policy and onto landlord coverage, with disclosure, liability, and evidence gates.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Week labels order the practitioner gates; no speaker testified to specific durations beyond the 15-minute conversion call. Premium figures are a Michigan quote and a national estimate.
diagrams.note: Drawn from Real Property Management Palisade (aUKpl6xobwU), Hannigan Insurance Agency (aGvo7Dq3gTM), Steadily (8qVhmrP1DZM), The CoLiving Insider (RyLyOzBiWEs), Blue Fox Properties (7sscnFcWkp4), Jacob and Elissa (ZoPbBZvfW94), and AmericanModernIns (fR49bewBEuo).

weeks.title: Make the conversion call
weeks.deliverable: A 15-minute call telling the agent the address is becoming a rental, before the tenant moves in.
weeks.gate: Policy rewritten for tenant occupancy; the failure mode is a denied claim.

weeks.title: Rewrite as a landlord policy
weeks.deliverable: Dwelling fire pushed to DP3 with replacement cost, loss of rent, vandalism, and water; about $1,200 a year versus $895 in Michigan, about 25 percent more per Steadily.
weeks.gate: Named insured matches how the home is deeded, including an LLC.

weeks.title: Disclose exact use and stack liability
weeks.deliverable: Written disclosure of rent-by-the-room use and at least $500,000 in liability; Lopez v. Allstate rescinded a policy on an about $371,000 loss.
weeks.gate: Every change in rooms or guest type reported before renewal.

weeks.title: Safety fixes and damage evidence
weeks.deliverable: Working smoke alarms, no dual cylinder deadbolts, screens on operable windows, and cleaner photos before every check-in and after every checkout.
weeks.gate: Scaled portfolios consolidate up to 30 homes on one bill and renewal date.
